name: Purpose strings and review rejection
plain: Every iOS privacy prompt needs a written reason in the app, or the app is rejected or crashes.
meaning: The string is the only text the person sees about why. Apple reviewers reject vague ones, and a missing key crashes the app.

android.store_policy: Play: Data safety form and permission declarations
android.note: No system purpose text; Data safety form is declared in Play Console

ios.prompt_ui: Prompt text comes from the key
ios.note: Missing key for a used API terminates the app; privacy manifests required from spring 2024

limits.headline: Can't ask for iPhone access without a written reason shown in the prompt
limits.user_action: Nothing. You see the reason when the app first asks for a camera, location or photos
can: Show you a sentence explaining why it wants an item, on iPhone
Show its own explanation before an Android permission box
Ask again later only if the reason text exists
cannot: Ask for a protected item on iPhone with no reason text; the app would close
Pass App Store review with a vague reason such as We need this
Change the reason text after release without a new app version
limits.reach_label: One sentence you see before choosing
limits.differs: iPhone requires the reason text in the app. Android has no system reason text; the developer fills a Data safety form in Play Console instead.

story.what_it_is: A short written reason an iOS app must show before it asks for something private.

marketing.name: Purpose strings
marketing.pitch: Explain in plain words why your app needs access, so people can decide.

story.for_you: The permission pop up has one sentence from the app explaining why it wants your camera, location or contacts. That sentence is often your only clue about what you are agreeing to.
story.for_makers: Apple will reject an app if the reason is vague, and the app crashes if the reason is missing. Good makers write clear sentences that raise yes rates, because people say yes when they see a real benefit.

use_cases.example: A rideshare app writes 'Your location is used to show nearby drivers' so the Allow button feels fair.
A photo sharing app says 'We need camera access so you can post photos' and avoids a rejection.
An AR game explains the camera use as 'to place creatures in your world', which lifts tap through on Allow.
A dating app writes why it wants location before it shows matches nearby.
A running app writes 'We track your route while you run, even when the screen is off' for the background location prompt.
An app review team bounces a build because the microphone string only said 'Microphone needed'.

story.android_note: Android has no required explanation text, though Google Play asks for a reason in review forms.
story.ios_note: iOS requires one text key for each private feature and shows it in the system prompt.

technical_bounds: Data safety form on Google Play

history.change: Purpose strings required for privacy APIs, crash if missing
Privacy manifests and required reason APIs enforced
